label: A pure favouring determination makes exactly the verdicts of its formal object
paraphrase: OPEN analyst bridge, attribution deferred: for every bearer b and every favouring profile phi such that the favouring determination of phi is a real determination of b, if that determination is a pure perfection (DEF-PURE-PERFECTION, the same purity parameter as the #2153 premises), then in every variation scenario phi favours x over y exactly when phi's formal object for b ranks x over y. The formal object is indexed by the bearer because one profile can belong to bearers of different kinds: Lane 2b's D-directed nature and determined will are the same function, which a natural bearer would have measured by its end and a willing bearer by the good. It is intended as the ranking that measures b's kind of operation, not phi's particular content; the Lean parameter does not enforce that, and with phi as its own object the bridge would be trivial. It is lane P's per-bearer reading of the loss and arbitrariness bridges taken together. It does not fix which standard that is, and it says nothing about whether the favouring is a natural or a rational appetite. With every favouring measured by value it follows from the two value-sense bridges 720bccc2 and a141e6a8 (valueBridgesArePerBearerConstant, Lean-only, with excluded middle) and gives their verdicts for every favouring some bearer has (perBearerConstantGivesValueBridges, Lean-only). Lane 2b's D-directed nature, measured by its own end, satisfies it (formalObjectControls row 5).
